title: Film checks feed later retrieval
statement: Feed students' answers to a film's in-video checks into the next lesson's retrieval, designing film and lesson together, without repeating what the current lesson's retrieval asks.
example: One unit's video design asks for three pause-answer-resume checks whose answers feed its second lesson's retrieval.
detail: Review of one unit's design material found it specifies a teaching sequence in which answers at the film's checks feed later retrieval, and its video brief asks for three pause, answer and resume checks whose responses feed the second lesson's retrieval. The page built for the film left those checks to the interface, so the review asked that the cue points, response handling and retrieval handoff be agreed together.
against: It is specified in one unit's video design and not shown working: the hand-off was still listed as open on 6 October (`g9/library/TIMELINE.md`, line 95).

evidence.quote: It specifies a teaching sequence, including video-check answers feeding later retrieval
three pause–answer–resume checks, with responses feeding Lesson 2 retrieval
